meta.purpose: 12px/18px short timestamps, token counts, status, file extensions, and compact names. Token estimates use the body family and tabular numerals.

control.purpose: 14px/21px buttons, menus, labels, short fields, explanatory text, and overview summary previews. The same role is used across surfaces.

body.purpose: 16px/28px normal-weight questions, answers, activity prose, notes, source reading, and multiline editors. Card and panel reading and editing use the same role and CJK fallback stack.

title.purpose: 16px/24px at weight 600 for card, panel, and overview names and name editors. Overview names retain bounded zoom compensation.

heading.purpose: 18px/27px at weight 600 for Markdown h3 headings across reading surfaces.

section.purpose: 20px/28px at weight 600 for large dialog titles and Markdown h2 headings.

page.purpose: 24px/32px at weight 600 for page titles and Markdown h1 headings.

mono.purpose: Family for code, file extensions, and technical identifiers; choose the size from the corresponding semantic role.

narrative.overview:
ThoughtDAG is an editable conversation canvas: readable question-and-answer cards, directional context edges, and a continuous reading panel. Cool neutral canvas controls keep graph structure legible; purple identifies mainline edges and selection, and orange identifies exploration. Conversation cards and the reading panel share the canvas tool cards' surface and boundary roles, with right-aligned blue user messages and plain assistant text.

This documents the implemented visual system, not a completed accessibility audit or a claim that every detail was individually approved. Rounded corners are welcome when outlines, dividers, and accents join coherently.
keyCharacteristics: Stable graph geometry across interaction and appearance.
Compact controls, readable content, and restrained overlay depth.
Distinct start, note, and file identities at every semantic zoom tier.
rules: Action toolbar: 16px group gaps and 4px related-control gaps; selection uses text in full layouts and accessible icons when compact, with no filled track or visible group caption. Selected/open/non-default controls share accent/9% fill while retaining correct ARIA semantics. Search has a 40px input row, 14px regular input text, a short placeholder, a single focus boundary, no shadow, and 14px keyboard hints only below results.

Layout inspector follows More and Object Format: shared canvas-tool-panel colors and outline; 16px horizontal/12px vertical content padding, 12px group gaps, 6px label spacing. Segments use More's single 6px-radius border with internal dividers, 14px text, 6px vertical padding, and accent/10 selected fill with accent text at 500 weight. No inset track or separate selected tile. Footer uses 8px padding/4px gaps, plain 32px-minimum Cancel and Preview buttons, and Object Format's filled Apply style.

Editing and dismissal: reversible short names and node/frame geometry save on Enter or leaving their editing boundary; Tab between geometry fields does not save and Escape cancels pending input. Connection purpose, routing and annotations save immediately without Apply/Cancel controls or a preview overlay; each choice and each continuous label edit is undoable. Content editors suspend with session drafts, including empty drafts. Escape exits only the top layer without submitting pending content; sending, generation, authorization, deletion and other configuration submission require explicit action. See docs/reference/interaction-contract.md and reuse the shared dismiss hooks.

Canvas spacing: 16px viewport and content insets, 8px toolbar padding, 4px control gaps, 32px controls, 12px section spacing. Compact overview names use 8px padding with the same zoom compensation as their text. Top control groups stay on a 50px single row, shortening labels and moving secondary entries into More as available canvas width decreases. Their 15px outer radius equals the 6px control radius plus 8px inset and 1px border. Project and source-session controls are borderless at rest; model connection keeps an accent fill without a nested outline.

Node proportions: conversation headers have a 52px minimum height, 12px 16px padding, 10px column gaps, and 28px controls; 12px working ports and 16px overview ports; Shared resize marks use 2px by 14px edge lines and a 14px two-line diagonal corner inset by 6px, with neutral resting color and accent hover/focus/drag states. Single-node marks follow canvas zoom with transparent 32px screen-space targets; multi-selection reuses the marks on its screen-space boundary and hides individual controls. Short-card width targets avoid side ports; wiring and sizing controls yield to the active gesture. Arrowheads use canvas coordinates independently of stroke thickness. First-question inputs group 16px search and send icons in a padded composer with 32px actions.

Conversation surfaces: thought cards and the focus panel alias the shared card, line, ink-muted, and wash roles used by More and Object Format, with blue right-aligned user messages and plain assistant text. The node radius aliases the 14px panel radius; headers and summary ends use 13px inner corners. User bubbles use 8px content corners with a 4px lower-right tag corner; code blocks, editors, and composers use 8px, while metadata actions use 6px control corners. Metadata is a full-width section with a bottom divider and a 40% composer-tone background. Its 38px disclosure stays folded in full view and becomes the name-and-summary preview in summary view. Metadata uses 16px horizontal insets; expanded fields have 12px gaps and 8px 0 12px padding, transparent backgrounds, and no inner border or radius. The conversation body and summary preview use 16px padding on every side. User bubbles use 12px 16px padding and a 16px gap before the answer, with no extra top margin. The focus header has a 56px minimum height and 12px 16px padding; scrolling content has 12px vertical padding, and all reading sections, metadata, and inspection sections share 16px horizontal insets. Metadata ends with a 12px gap, and question and answer sections each end with 16px. Narrow panels retain these insets and bubble padding while widening user messages to 94%. AI fill edits session drafts; only explicit Save commits them. Summary type and insets divide by canvas zoom clamped from 0.32 to 1. Material identities retain their existing palettes; compact overview corners keep their zoom-compensated form. The draggable header shows complete tokens text immediately followed by a wrench and the tool-call count on the same line, separated by 12px. The 6px-high composition bar with a continuous 1px neutral perimeter below matches the whole group width, with a 104px minimum group width. One block element paints all segments as a hard-stop linear gradient with identical adjacent stop positions. Colors are clipped to the padding box inside a continuous 1px neutral perimeter, keeping their transitions away from the shared outside contour at fractional canvas scales. The tool indicator displays only its wrench icon and count. The total, icon, count, and bar are static metadata with no hover, focus, or click popup and no additional keyboard stop. They remain drag targets. The estimate includes saved question, answer, tool records, and recorded thinking; it excludes other attachments and upstream context and is not API billing usage. Missing thinking contributes no invented segment.

Typography uses purpose-based shared roles from src/index.css: meta 12px/18px, control 14px/21px, body 16px/28px, title 16px/24px, heading 18px/27px, section 20px/28px, and page 24px/32px at the default root size. Titles use weight 600; body and metadata use 400. Questions, answers, activity prose, notes, and multiline editors use body across canvas cards and focus panels. Controls and explanations use control, while short counts and dates use meta. Full cards at 100% zoom match the reading panel. Markdown h1/h2/h3 use page/section/heading consistently. Narrow surfaces reflow rather than shrink labels.

Overview names use title at 16px, summary previews use control at 14px, and compact names and file identities use meta at 12px. Summary previews intentionally differ from full 16px multiline editors. Existing zoom compensation retains the summary 0.32-to-1 clamp and compact 0.22 lower clamp, allowing smaller apparent text only at extreme canvas distances. Exported .tmap-art artwork, tutorial SVG diagrams, and timeline ladder dynamic text retain separate coordinate-dependent type scales.
dos: Do use the semantic radius tokens and a continuous card outline.
Do preserve context-arrow order and vertical alignment within each conversation chain.
Do keep top-left project and session controls aligned at the same height.
Do retain node names and file extensions when reducing visual detail.
Do use actual filenames, extensions, and available file sizes.
Do verify light and dark appearances without changing component geometry.
Do use the shared semantic typography roles for the same purpose across cards, panels, menus, and settings, including reading and editing states.
donts: Don't replace coherent rounded corners with an all-square interface.
Don't add a detached decorative stripe that breaks a card's outline.
Don't translate nodes on hover or clip their external connection ports.
Don't add stacked shadows to the minimap or turn its viewport mask into a dark slab.
Don't nest raised cards throughout the focus panel's reading area.
Don't invent file metadata, previews, or promotional third-party UI copy.
Don't introduce component-specific font sizes or smaller labels to fit narrow application surfaces.
